      <title>ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted</title>

      <description><p>Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result</p><p>The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.</p><p>Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 13:40:33 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Americas</category><title>Trump’s stillborn diesel deal: Why Russian oil tankers are not heading to the US</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261106-trump-stillborn-diesel-deal-why-russian-oil-tankers-are-not-heading-to-the-us</link><description>
The first oil tankers scheduled to deliver Russian diesel to the US under a deal between President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin have changed course and are no longer heading toward the US coast. It spells the end of an agreement announced with great fanfare before the midterms.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/583fe45e-d93a-11f1-9d4e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/image-tanker-diesel3.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/583fe45e-d93a-11f1-9d4e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/image-tanker-diesel3.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72572b5c-d9d7-11f1-aa8a-15a9cc0740e7</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 13:38:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/583fe45e-d93a-11f1-9d4e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/image-tanker-diesel3.png">© Studio graphique France Médias Monde</source><dc:creator>Sébastian SEIBT</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Is Israel opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot going to replace Benjamin Netanyahu?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261106-is-israel-opposition-figure-gadi-eisenkot-going-to-replace-benjamin-netanyahu</link><description>
In Israel, Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday, November 5, as the frontrunner to be tasked with forming a government. This comes after one of the two main parties representing ultra-Orthodox Jewish voters – a longtime ally of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition – declined to recommend any candidate for the task. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Jerusalem Noga Tarnopolsky reports.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ebb71fde-d9cd-11f1-a086-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-04af7880.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ebb71fde-d9cd-11f1-a086-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-04af7880.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8163f792-d9cd-11f1-b042-e7fb1d136a6b</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 13:25:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's future in question after midterms setback</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261106-us-defence-secretary-pete-hegseth-s-future-in-question-after-midterms-setback</link><description>
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's future is in question after Tuesday's, November 3, midterms setback. On Thursday, November 5, he issued a video message vowing to fight efforts in Congress to impeach him and defending the ‌Iran war as “courageous and historic”. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle has more.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/786ab9d8-d9d6-11f1-88c5-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-bcc8d7a2.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/786ab9d8-d9d6-11f1-88c5-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-bcc8d7a2.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ee8dbbc0-d9d5-11f1-bdf5-e56d28bb9ded</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 13:15:54 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Tech giants lose $1 trillion in one day after Democrats victory in midterms</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261106-tech-giants-lose-1-trillion-in-one-day-after-democrats-victory-in-midterms</link><description>
Trillions of dollars have been wiped off the stock value of major tech firms in the US, Europe and Asia. Investors appear worried about the possibility of an AI slowdown and tougher regulation as Democrats won the midterms in the US. Some of the Democratic candidates had expressed their opposition to the data centres that are needed to power AI technology.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6e1d77ee-d9dc-11f1-9d72-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-4f9220cf.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6e1d77ee-d9dc-11f1-9d72-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-4f9220cf.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0d57022c-d9dc-11f1-817e-cfc74dac3b1b</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 13:15:27 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Canada PM Mark Carney unveils budget to strengthen economy</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261106-canada-pm-mark-carney-unveils-budget-to-strengthen-economy</link><description>

]]> <![CDATA[ Northern lights could reach New York and Idaho this weekend as speedy solar wind races toward Earth ]]> The northern lights could put on an impressive display this weekend as a colossal coronal hole on the sun fires a stream of high-speed solar wind toward Earth.

Minor (G1) geomagnetic storm conditions between Nov. 6 and Nov. 8, with a chance of moderate (G2) conditions on Nov. 7 and Nov. 8, according to NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC).

If G2 conditions materialize, the northern lights could be visible as far south as New York and Idaho.

What is happening?

The culprit behind the potential uptick in northern lights is a large coronal hole on the sun, a region where the sun's magnetic field opens up. They allow streams of charged particles known as the solar wind to escape more easily into space. Coronal holes appear darker in ultraviolet images because they are cooler and less dense than their surroundings.

And this particularly large — and rather oddly shaped — coronal hole is sending some seriously speedy wind our way.

The U.K. Met Office forecasts solar wind speeds between 342 and 404 miles (550-650 kilometers) per second, considerably faster than the typical speed of around 249 miles (400 km) per second.

The fast solar winds are expected to arrive around Nov. 6-7 and could persist through much of the weekend. It could interact with Earth's magnetic field, potentially triggering geomagnetic storms and fueling spectacular aurora shows. The stronger the storm, the farther south the northern lights can potentially be seen.

Where will auroras be visible?

Under G1 conditions, auroras may be visible from northern Michigan and Maine, but if activity intensifies to G2 levels, skywatchers farther south, including those in New York and Idaho, could be in for a treat.

But remember! Aurora forecasts are notoriously tricky. Much depends on the strength and orientation of the magnetic field carried by the incoming solar wind, particularly whether it points southward, allowing more energy to transfer to Earth's magnetic field.

Northern Hemisphere aurora forecast courtesy of the U.K. Met Office

To give yourself the best chance of seeing the northern lights, keep an eye on those aurora forecasts, head somewhere dark away from city lights if you can, with a view of the northern horizon.

To stay updated on space weather and know the best times and places to catch auroras, consider using a space weather app tailored to your location. One app I recommend is "My Aurora Forecast & Alerts," available on both iOS and Android. Another great tool is the "Space Weather Live" app on iOS and Android, which offers more in-depth insights into current space weather conditions and their potential for aurora activity.

]]> <![CDATA[ Max Power: NASA hosting its 1st air show this weekend on Florida's Space Coast ]]> NASA will host a first-of-its-kind air show and aerospace expo on Florida's Space Coast this weekend.

The show, called Max Power, will take place Saturday and Sunday (Nov. 7 and Nov. 8) at and around NASA's Kennedy Space Center (KSC). That name should be familiar to "Simpsons" fans, by the way: Max Power is an alias that Homer uses in the 13th episode of the show's 10th season. (He got it off a hair dryer.)

There will be a lot to see at NASA's event, so you should consider dropping by if you're on the Space Coast this weekend. (Tickets are required; you can buy them here.) Here are a few of the highlights.

Saturday, Nov. 7 (all times local, EST):

  • 11:15-11:30 a.m.: Overview of NASA's "quiet" supersonic jet, the X-59
  • 12:30-1:00 p.m.: Discussion of NASA's science and exploration goals by Nicky Fox and Lori Glaze (the heads of NASA's Science Mission Directorate and Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate, respectively)
  • 12:45-1:00 p.m.: Q&A with the four astronauts of NASA's Artemis III mission
  • 1:00-1:30 p.m.: "How Is NASA Preparing Astronauts to Live and Work on the Moon?" with Suzanne Bell, who leads NASA’s Behavioral Health and Performance Laboratory at Johnson Space Center
  • 1:30-2:00 p.m.: Discussion of NASA's planned lunar outpost, with Moon Base program head Carlos García-Galán
  • 2:00-2:30 p.m.: Summary of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope mission, by senior project scientist Julie McEnery

Sunday, Nov. 8

  • 11:15-11:30 a.m.: "How NASA uses aircraft for research! Topic: Connecting flight to research"
  • 12:45-1:15 p.m.: Update on the U.S. Space Academy with NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson

  • 1:00-1:30 p.m.: Discussion of SR-1 Freedom, NASA's planned nuclear-powered spacecraft that will launch mini-helicopters to Mars in 2028
  • 1:30-2:00 p.m.: "The X-Factor: NASA's Flight Revolution Topic: X-Planes"
  • 2:00-2:30 p.m.: Conversation with an (as yet unnamed) NASA astronaut
  • 3:00-3:15: "In the Cockpit: Meet the NASA Pilots!"

NASA will also hold a livestreamed press conference on Saturday at 5 p.m. EST (2200 GMT) about its moon base plans. It will feature Fox, García-Galán, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and Dayna Ise, the acting director of the Utility and Infrastructure Office for the Moon Base Program.

"NASA will display its quiet supersonic X-59 plane, and agency partners will showcase moon rovers, spacecraft and more."

The meteorite, named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered in 2022, weighs roughly 1.8 pounds (800 grams) and formed more than 4.1 billion years ago. Blasted off Mars by an impact before eventually landing on Earth, it is one of the three oldest Martian meteorites ever found.

The extraordinary age and unusual mineral composition of Teghaza 001 offer a rare glimpse into the formation of Mars' early crust and how volcanic materials may have been altered by water, according to a statement from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California.

"It was only after we started looking closely that we realized this meteorite is really unique,” research leader Yang Liu of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California said in the statement. "One of the paper’s reviewers called it a Rosetta Stone for Mars."

A Rosetta Stone for Mars

Unlike many Martian meteorites, Teghaza 001 contains a distinctive combination of igneous minerals and textures that preserve evidence of its complex history. Its mineral composition resembles materials observed in Mars' southern highlands by NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.

Although researchers can’t pinpoint exactly where the meteorite originated on Mars, they have identified 13 potential locations on the planet where it may have formed.

"This is really our first piece of Martian crust from a part of Mars we’ve never had a sample of before," team member Lee Saper, NASA’s Ames Research Center in Silicon Valley, said. "It records interactions of water and rock and maybe even an imprint of the Martian atmosphere as it was losing water."

The meteorite was initially identified as Martian based on its oxygen isotopes. To determine its age, scientists then examined tiny zircon crystals embedded in the rock. Using a specialized rubidium-strontium dating technique, researchers analyzed individual mineral grains on its surface, preserving it for future analysis.

The mineral and chemical evidence points to a dynamic water cycle on ancient Mars, when liquid water interacted with the planet's crust and potentially left traces of its atmosphere as it gradually lost water.

Scientists believe further analysis of Teghaza 001 could reveal more about how water shaped the Martian surface and influenced the planet's evolution. The study also marks the first time researchers have used rubidium-strontium dating to analyze an ancient Martian meteorite, opening the door for the technique to be applied to other samples in the future.

"We've only scratched the surface," Liu concluded.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays ]]> Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate "Max Power" on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same.

The two retrieved the 750-pound (340 kilograms) iROSA assembly from a temporary stowage platform, carried it to the worksite by way of the Canadarm2 robotic arm and mounted it to its previously assembled bracket kit.

Menon then attached the cables to tie the iROSA into the station's systems but ran into a problem.

"We are seeing half of the expected shunt current that we want," radioed Nichole Stilwell, a NASA astronaut serving as the spacewalk officer in Mission Control. "In this current config, we are not necessarily going to deploy."

To address the issue, the connectors needed to be inspected. Out of safety concerns — given that the arrays generate electricity whenever lit by the sun — the astronauts needed to wait for the space station to enter the shadow of Earth to see what could be done. In the interim, they spent the time cleaning up their worksite and returning the Canadarm2 to its park site as they would have done after the deployment.

Fortunately, they were able to clear the issue.

"We are seeing good shunt currents on the ground, so we are go for deploy," said Stilwell.

After releasing two bolts, Kutryk and Menon watched as the array started to unfurl to its full 63-foot (19 meters) length. No motor was needed; the iROSA, as designed, used only the potential energy stored by its rolled-up carbon composite booms to extend itself. The entire process took about 10 minutes.

Beginning in June 2021, four teams of two astronauts did as was done on Thursday to deploy each array. ]]> <![CDATA[ Andy Weir says his new sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' is a way to 'revive the old art of radio plays' (interview) ]]> Hot off the tremendous theatrical success of this year's "Project Hail Mary," adapted from Andy Weir's 2021 novel of the same name, the New York Times bestselling author is rocketing back into deep space with a brand new Audible Original release landing on Nov. 5, 2026, titled "Exoplanet."

Weir ("The Martian") is executive producing this ambitious full-cast audiobook drama with acclaimed author and ace comic writer Benjamin Percy ("Wolverine") for the first in a series of curated sci-fi projects for Amazon's Audible.

The seven-episode sci-fi thriller stars the vocal talents of Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo in a wild time-travel space disaster odyssey that also benefits from Lucasfilm’s Skywalker Sound, which provided the show’s immersive acoustic elements.

"One crew. One planet. Three timelines. No one survives alone," states the official synopsis. "When a quantum anomaly tears apart the starship Wild Blue Yonder, each surviving crew member crash-lands in a different era on the same deadly exoplanet—hunted, alone, and running out of time."

Ahead of the audio drama's launch, we sat down with Weir and Percy to find out more about this exciting science fiction adventure.

When Percy was first approached by Audible about this challenging endeavor, it was part of a bake-off situation where he was competing with several other writers, all jockeying for position.

"I think the thing that set me apart is my understanding of how to channel legacy properties," Percy tells Space. "Having written for DC and for Marvel, I can take 'Star Wars' or 'Predator' or Wolverine or Batman and honor that legacy but also put my own unique spin on it.

"When it came to the banner of 'Andy Weir Presents,' my job was to write my best version of an awesome Andy Weir story. So I thought about space disasters, big-hearted hopefulness, quippy humor, and a roller coaster plot, and then I nested into all of that a time-travel story."

Writing an audio drama is unlike the comic work that Percy is known for, but as he explains, it's also quite different from working on conventional shows and movies too.

"If you’re watching TV or film, you’re passive and letting it wash over you. You’re taking in the story as a passenger," notes Percy. "But when you're listening to audio, you're invited in with the dialogue, the narration, the sound cues. You’re invited to fill in the vacancies. As a result of that, you become like a co-author in the experience. I was super excited to jump into this project."

The genesis of "Exoplanet" started with Audible approaching Weir with the basic idea, but what they didn't know was that he had already been thinking about resurrecting great radio dramas of the past.

"Earlier on in my life, even before 'The Martian,' I wanted to bring back audio-only entertainment with full-cast productions and sound effects," shares Weir. "I got into listening to things like 'The Lone Ranger' and 'The Shadow' and, of course, the Basil Rathbone Sherlock Holmes adaptations. As Weir points out, he's thankfully not the one wielding the pen this time around, but he did select Percy to be his champion.

"We got a bunch of different story concepts submitted to us from lots of talented authors, and Ben's was the one that stood out head and shoulders above the rest. It’s a really interesting concept," says Weir.

The space rock, designated 2026 QQ8, was first observed in August 2026 after entering orbit around Earth in April 2026. The discovery was reported by the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center on Thursday (Oct. 29).

The stay of QQ8 is a temporary one. The mini-moon will remain in the thrall of Earth's gravity through December before breaking away in 2027.

Scientists have recreated the orbital path of QQ8, finding that it takes 359 days, or about 0.98 of an Earth year, to orbit the sun. QQ8 closely approaches Earth around once every ten years, but this time the object came so close that Earth has been able to gravitationally seize it.

According to the Minor Planet Center, the closest QQ8 will come to our planet during this stay is around 353,000 miles (568,000 kilometers). That is around 110,000 miles (177,000 km) further out than the average distance between Earth and the moon.

Even if QQ8 were to come close enough to collide with Earth, it would likely be completely destroyed in our planet's atmosphere before it reaches the surface, as it is only around 6 feet (2 meters) in diameter.

This is far from the first time Earth has snagged itself a mini-moon, more accurately called a temporary satellite. In fact, research last year suggested that our planet could be orbited by as many as six mini-moons at any given time, with many of these being fragments of our more permanent natural satellite, the moon.

While QQ8 is tiny, it is larger than the average mini-moon. That is according to modelling earlier this year that suggested the average size for a temporary satellite is 75 centimeters (30 inches) across.

The same modelling suggested the average stay for such an object would be around nine months.

So if QQ8 was captured in April 2026, that means it should move away in January 2027.

The researchers behind those findings suggested that, were Earth to gravitationally grip a space rock around 10 feet (3 meters) wide, it could serve as a mini-moon for 10 to 20 years.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 5, 2002: NASA's Galileo spacecraft flies by Jupiter moon Amalthea only to find it's a 'pile of icy rubble less dense than water' ]]>

On Nov. 5, 2002, NASA's old Galileo spacecraft was almost out of fuel. But the Jupiter mission still had some science to do. Galileo flew by a small moon called Amalthea. Amalthea is small, but it's interesting for scientists.

The Jupiter moon Amalthea is the reddest object in our solar system. It also generates more heat than it gets from the sun. Scientists think Amalthea creates electrical currents as it orbits in Jupiter's huge magnetic field. Near this little moon, strong radiation from Jupiter is dangerous for spacecraft.

The flyby caused some problems for Galileo. The spacecraft went into safe mode only 30 minutes after going past Amalthea. NASA said it was ready for problems, because Galileo was on its last legs, and the radiation near Amalthea was strong. However, NASA quickly fixed the problem and got Galileo working again.

Less than a year later, Galileo threw itself into Jupiter's atmosphere. The spacecraft was crushed by the high pressure in Jupiter's atmosphere, but its data still survives on Earth.

Why it mattered

The Galileo spacecraft was running on cosmic fumes by the time it reached Amalthea and the flyby would be the last time the probe would ever swing by one of Jupiter's moons.

While it may not look like it in Galileo's black and white images above and below, Amalthea is tinted red due sulfur contamination on its surface. The moon is small, about 168 miles long, and orbits about 112,468 miles (181,000 km) from Jupiter (much closer to the planet than the Earth and its moon).

Galileo flew within 99 miles of Amalthea during its flyby, which also marked the closest Galileo would get to Jupiter before its death dive in September 2005.

"Scientists studying data from NASA's Galileo spacecraft have found that Jupiter's moon Amalthea is a pile of icy rubble less dense than water," NASA announced in May 2005

"Amalthea is throwing us a curve ball," Torrence Johnson, a study co-author on the Almathea flyby and project scientist for the Galileo mission at JPL, said in 2005. "Its density is well below that of water ice, and even with substantial porosity, Amalthea probably contains a lot of water ice, as well as rock."

Originally known as Jupiter V (because it was the fifth Jupiter moon discovered after the so-called Galilean moons Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto), Amalthea was named after naiad, or water nymph, from Greek mythology.

It is fitting that Amalthea was the last of Jupiter's moons to be visited by the Galileo spacecraft. The moon was also last Jupiter moon to be discovered by visual observations when it was first disovered by astronomer Edward Emerson Barnard in September 1892 using the Lick Observatory telescope in California.

The Galileo spacecraft ultimately crashed into Jupiter on Sept. 21, 2005, less than a year after its Amalthea flyby.

   <description>Slunečné dny vystřídají mrazivá rána a na mnoha místech bude panovat i vytrvalá nízká oblačnost. Příjemné denní teploty a sluneční paprsky ale dlouho nevydrží. Už v pondělí se začne počasí měnit. Od západu přibude oblačnosti a postupně by se měly přidat i srážky.</description>

   <description>Na bolesti v oblasti zad a krku si občas stěžuje takřka každý. Šíjové svaly kvůli neustálému hledění na mobil či práci na počítači totiž trápí i lidi, kteří dlouhodobé ani vážnější problémy s krční či hrudní páteří nemají. Běžné bolesti napraví vhodné cviky, při přetrvávajících potížích, které se při dlouhých večerech strávených s mobilem pravidelně projeví hned po probuzení, je podle odborníků důležité navštívit lékaře či fyzioterapeuta, který stanoví vhodný postup.</description>

   <title>Black Friday ukrývá i falešné slevy. Jak odhalit triky obchodníků a nenaletět</title>

   <description>Nákupní období kolem Black Friday v Česku naplno propuklo. Tradiční termín letos ve světě připadá na 27. listopadu, většina velkých online prodejců u nás však již své masivní slevové kampaně spustila. Spotřebitelské organizace varují před psychologickým nátlakem a triky e-shopů a poukazují i na blížící se velkou novinku u nákupů na internetu. Od roku 2027 začne se zpožděním platit takzvaná tlačítková novela. Zjednoduší zákazníkům vrácení zboží.</description>

 <description>Rusko zabavilo od začátku války desítky ukrajinských hotelů. Majitel hotelu tak zřejmě vede předem prohraný boj.</description>

Kraj je v tomto týdnu předal organizaci Post Bellum, která zajistí jejich dopravu do země zasažené ruskou agresí. Kraj tak navazuje na loňskou pomoc, celkově daroval už osm těchto vozů.</description></item><item><title>Víkend bude slunečný, zaprší až příští týden</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905058-vikend-bude-slunecny-zaprsi-az-pristi-tyden.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905058-vikend-bude-slunecny-zaprsi-az-pristi-tyden.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Počasí v Libereckém kraji slibuje na víkend sice poměrně nízké teploty, ale slunečné počasí. Teploty k ránu klesnou i pod minus tři stupně, přes den se pak vyšplhají k osmi stupňům. Srážky podle meteorologů přijdou až příští týden.</description></item><item><title>Mrazivá noc na Jizerce: Zdejší stanice naměřila nejnižší teplotu v Česku</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905060-mraziva-noc-na-jizerce-zdejsi-stanice-namerila-nejnizsi-teplotu-v-cesku.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905060-mraziva-noc-na-jizerce-zdejsi-stanice-namerila-nejnizsi-teplotu-v-cesku.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 08:58:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Absolutním mrazovým rekordmanem pátku 6. listopadu se stala Jizerka v Libereckém kraji, kde teplota klesla až na -10,3 °C. Mrazivá noc zasáhla většinu republiky, podle Českého hydrometeorologického ústavu zaznamenalo 90 procent měřicích stanic teploty pod bodem mrazu.</description></item><item><title>Čeští vojáci mění maskování. Na novém maskovacím vzoru a zároveň rozsáhlém projektu MAD21 spolupracovala s armádou i Technická univerzita v Liberci.</description></item><item><title>Jablonec veze z Rigy bod za remízu 1:1, vyrovnával Nebyla</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/905045-jablonec-veze-z-rigy-bod-za-remizu-1-1-vyrovnaval-nebyla.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/905045-jablonec-veze-z-rigy-bod-za-remizu-1-1-vyrovnaval-nebyla.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 23:13:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Jablonečtí fotbalisté získali ve 3. kole ligové fáze Konferenční ligy UEFA druhý bod za remízu 1:1 s lotyšským FC Riga. Ve středu 4. listopadu 2026 se ve sportovní hale ve Varnsdorfu uskutečnilo okresní kolo florbalového turnaje ČEPS Cupu, určeného pro žáky 1.–5. tříd základních škol.

Turnaj se hrál systémem 3 + 1. Každý tým se utkal s každým soupeřem dvoukolově, přičemž jedno utkání trvalo 2 × 8 minut. Na turnaji se představily tři týmy – ZŠ Východní, Centrum dětí a mládeže Česká Kamenice a naše škola. Každý tým tak odehrál celkem čtyři utkání. Vítězný tým turnaje postoupí do krajského finále.

Hned v úvodním utkání nás čekal nejtěžší soupeř, domácí ZŠ Východní. Po velmi vyrovnaném a bojovném průběhu jsme dokázali zvítězit těsným výsledkem 4:3. Druhý zápas proti soupeři z České Kamenice jsme zvládli výborně a po přesvědčivém výkonu jsme zvítězili 6:2. Ve druhém kole jsme se znovu utkali se ZŠ Východní. Tentokrát nám soupeř porážku oplatil a po dramatickém průběhu jsme prohráli nejtěsnějším rozdílem 2:3. Jelikož i ZŠ Východní zvítězila nad Českou Kamenicí, bylo před závěrečným utkáním jasné, že o vítězi turnaje rozhodne počet vstřelených branek proti tomuto soupeři.

Do závěrečného utkání jsme proto nastoupili s jasnou taktikou – vstřelit co nejvíce branek. Po většinu turnaje nás v brance skvěle držel Adam Reichert, který několika výbornými zákroky podržel tým v nejtěžších chvílích. Pro rozhodující utkání jsme však zvolili odvážný taktický tah. Adama jsme přesunuli z branky do pole, protože sehraná trojice Adam Reichert, Hugo Bláha a Dominik Košín měla za úkol nastřílet co nejvíce gólů. Tento plán dokonale vyšel. Našemu týmu se podařilo zvítězit vysokým rozdílem a vstřelit soupeři 13 branek, tedy o tři více, než dokázala ZŠ Východní. Díky lepšímu skóre jsme se stali vítězi okresního kola a vybojovali si zasloužený postup do krajského finále.

Velkou pochvalu si zaslouží celý tým za bojovnost, nasazení a kolektivní výkon. V našem týmu nastoupila také jediná dívka Barča Šeráková, která byla velmi platnou hráčkou a svým výkonem významně přispěla k celkovému úspěchu.
